root_cause_label: Hallucinated Repository URLs via Pattern-Based Guessing
one_sentence_failure_summary: After a bs4 dependency failure blocked web-search, the agent pivoted to fabricating GitHub URLs by guessing common naming patterns rather than installing the missing package or using an alternative search method.
t_err_evidence: In step 13, after the bs4 import failure in step 12, the agent rewrites the script to hardcode URLs based on 'common patterns' (e.g., https://github.com/STAIR-Lab/STAIR, https://github.com/locate3d/locate3d, https://github.com/inductive-moment-matching/imm) without any actual search or verification — these are fabricated plausible-sounding URLs.
t_commit_evidence: Step 13 writes these fabricated URLs into result.jsonl; from this point the output file contains the wrong answers and subsequent steps only verify the file's format, not the correctness of the URLs.
trigger_explanation: The real environment blocker was the missing bs4 module (step 12). Instead of resolving it (e.g., pip install bs4 or using curl for HTTP requests), the agent incorrectly handled the obstacle by pivoting to hallucinating repository URLs based on naming patterns, which is a fabrication strategy rather than a valid workaround.
forewarning_evidence: Step 12 produced ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'bs4', signaling that the intended search strategy was broken before the agent committed to hallucinating answers in step 13.
fabrication_evidence: Step 13 hardcodes URLs such as https://github.com/STAIR-Lab/STAIR, https://github.com/locate3d/locate3d, https://github.com/inductive-moment-matching/imm, https://github.com/cross-env-coop/cec, https://github.com/diffusion-purification/dap, and https://github.com/char-lm/character-lm — all fabricated by guessing naming patterns, with no real web search performed. Steps 14-17 only verify the JSONL format, not URL validity.
